questions.prompt: A stack follows which access discipline?
questions.explanation: A stack pushes and pops at the same end (the top), so the most recently added element is removed first — LIFO.

questions.prompt: Which Python container gives O(1) enqueue and dequeue for a FIFO queue?
questions.explanation: deque supports O(1) operations at both ends. A list's pop(0) is O(1)? No — it shifts every element and is O(n).

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Push/pop at the end of a Python list are O(1)
deque supports O(1) append and popleft
A stack is LIFO and a queue is FIFO
Using list.pop(0) as a dequeue is O(1)

questions.explanation: Lists are great stacks (O(1) at the end) and deques are great queues (O(1) both ends). list.pop(0) is O(n), so (d) is false.

questions.prompt: A queue serves elements in ______ order. (four-letter acronym)
questions.explanation: First In, First Out: the earliest-enqueued element is dequeued first.

questions.prompt: Values 1, 2, 3 are pushed onto a stack in that order, then popped. Order the values by when they are popped (first popped first).
questions.explanation: A stack is LIFO, so the last pushed (3) is popped first, then 2, then 1.

questions.prompt: Match each item with its property.
questions.explanation: Stacks are LIFO, queues are FIFO, deque is O(1) at both ends, and removing from the front of a list is O(n).
